correctness.rationale: Full-rank affine problem: group averaging shows the uniform edge-incidence barycenter is an optimal center. The complete Edmonds spanning-tree inequality system is checked via exact min and max support values. Deleting each selected induced-edge set gives exactly 0, a, or b unavoidable edges; reflected-support bounds reduce to \(p-1\), \(q-1\), and a monotone interior quotient, producing the exact closed formula. The balanced sign comparison is an elementary rational identity with strictly positive denominator. A standalone exact-rational program verifies all spanning-tree vertices and subset support ratios for eight parameter pairs, corroborating but not replacing the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected source by Pineda-Villavicencio and Schröter establishes matroid-polytope reconstructibility and discusses facet recovery, without a Minkowski-asymmetry value for \(K_{p,q}\). Chaourar establishes structural facet descriptions but not the reflected-support maximum. A graphic-matroid base polytope being a face of a larger one does not determine its asymmetry from geometric invariants of the larger body. Six actual semantic database queries and targeted literature searches found no dominating assertion; equivalence under another terminology remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: Evaluates an affine-invariant extremal geometric quantity for the entire two-parameter family of complete-bipartite graphic matroid base polytopes. Exact balance changes the controlling inequality class; only \(p=q\) has an additional positive asymmetry excess, which tends to 1/2 as dimensions grow. This structural transition and closed form are more than isolated numerical instances.
